scope: Every step of the two distinct T12 orientation examples: scientific case study and orientation interchange. Step indices are zero-based; this is not all OrientationAnalysis filters.

filters.purpose: Read the public CTF map and convert Euler angles to radians; the next step applies the default Oxford/HKL sample-frame correction.

Apply the documented default Oxford/HKL CTF correction: rotate the sample reference frame 180 degrees about Y before masks, quaternions and segmentation. No additional Euler-frame rotation is prescribed for this CTF/BCC input; retain the transform-derived origin.
Accept pixels only when Phases > 0 AND Error == 0. Keep rejected measurements in the saved arrays but exclude them from segmentation.
Convert radians-based Euler orientations to quaternions for symmetry-aware segmentation and feature averaging.
Join face-connected valid pixels within a phase when pairwise misorientation is below 5 degrees. Keep the finite map nonperiodic and feature IDs unrandomized.
Measure every positive feature before reporting selection. With one Z cell and unit Z spacing, the size output is area and the diameter is an equivalent circle diameter.
Compute one symmetry-aware Rodrigues average per positive feature as the fixed reference for later orientation-spread comparisons; do not average Euler components directly.
Select features with NumElements >= 4 for reporting, following the paper minimum population size. Retain smaller features and their pixel labels without reassignment.
Color accepted orientations relative to corrected sample Z for visual context; no loading-axis or strain inference is implied.
Save measured arrays, validity mask, unchanged segmentation, feature sizes, reporting mask, and average orientations as the shared checkpoint.

Radius [1, 1, 0] is the smallest nonzero in-plane baseline: a clipped 3 by 3 window with 0.5 micrometer axial reach. Feature mode tests matching positive FeatureIds; preparation makes each grain phase-coherent. Center and diagonal cells contribute. Output KAM_R1_Grain in degrees.
Compare each cell quaternion with its grain AvgQuats; save cell reference angles and per-grain mean spread in degrees.
Summarize KAM over indexed pixels; each admitted pixel contributes once.
Summarize grain-reference misorientation over indexed pixels; each admitted pixel contributes once.
Summarize one spread per reportable grain with at least four pixels; each grain contributes once.
Export positive Feature_ID rows with GrainOrientationSpread, ReportableFeatures, and unchanged feature measurements.
Save original T12 arrays plus cell maps, grain spread, and the three one-row masked summaries.
Increase only the same-grain kernel radius to [2, 2, 0]: a clipped 5 by 5 window with 1.0 micrometer axial reach. Save KAM_R2_Grain in degrees; retain the existing KAM_R1_Grain baseline.
Radius one, same-phase comparisons across positive feature IDs; save KAM_R1_Phase in degrees.
Summarize KAM_R1_Grain over IndexedPixels with one equally weighted observation per admitted pixel.
Summarize KAM_R2_Grain over IndexedPixels with one equally weighted observation per admitted pixel.
Summarize KAM_R1_Phase over IndexedPixels with one equally weighted observation per admitted pixel.
Save the complete case study: preparation arrays, local and grain-reference metrics, feature spread, all three KAM maps, and all six masked summaries.
Read the complete preparation checkpoint from (01) T12 Orientation Case Study; preserve its corrected geometry, measured arrays, mask, phases, and features.
Copy only EulerAngles before the in-place unit conversion; retain the original radians array.
Convert the copy from radians to degrees in place. All cells are processed; IndexedPixels still determines measurement validity.
Copy the degree array to retain both units while checking a return to radians.
Convert the second copy from degrees back to radians; expect float32 rounding, not a new orientation or frame.
Reorder scalar-last XYZW quaternions to scalar-first WXYZ for a consumer that explicitly expects that order; retain the original.
Reorder WXYZ back to XYZW; the result should match the original components exactly. No normalization, rotation, or symmetry operation occurs.
Conjugate the original scalar-last quaternion to [-x,-y,-z,w]. This represents the inverse only for a unit quaternion; it is not a frame correction.
Conjugate the scalar-last result again; expect exact original components while retaining the inverse branch for inspection.

Export original radians as degrees, keeping only indexed pixels and splitting by phase. T12 produces T12_IndexedAngles_Phase_1.txt in source tuple order, with weight 1 and sigma 1. This writes an angle file, not an ODF.
Save every original preparation object plus the six derived arrays with explicit units or component order in their names.
